summary: Iteration 54 testing complete. All 3 enhancements verified: Logo upload (5/5 backend + UI works), Email Templates CRUD + preview + reset (8/8 backend + UI renders all 4 templates with chips/save/preview/reset), SMTP Alerts (3/3 backend with proper RBAC). Found and FIXED one critical frontend bug: BrandingSettingsPage threw 'Upload is not defined' runtime error (missing import from lucide-react). All 22 backend pytest tests pass. Regression checks all green (2FA, compounds, audit-logs, analytics dashboard with real residents data, scheduler status, smtp-health stats).

minor.issue: Ignores 'period' field in JSON body — always queues 'previous-month'. Could not directly verify template substitution in actual run for a custom period like 2027-12. Template rendering itself was unit-tested via /preview endpoint (passes).

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED — Missing 'Upload' icon import from lucide-react caused 'Uncaught ReferenceError: Upload is not defined' runtime error breaking the entire /app/branding page

action_items: (Optional) Allow /api/reports/run-monthly-now to accept a 'period' override in body for QA/manual triggering of arbitrary months. Currently it always queues previous-month.
Consider adding ESLint rule no-undef for React components to catch missing icon imports at lint time.
critical_code_review_comments: BrandingSettingsPage.js: lint did not catch missing 'Upload' import — recommend running `yarn lint` in CI to prevent this class of bug.
email_templates.py PUT validates `subject and html` truthiness — passes for whitespace-only strings; consider .strip() check.
compound_branding.py upload_logo: file size check happens after full read — for very large uploads this loads all bytes into memory. Acceptable for 2MB cap.
smtp_alerts.py: cooldown query uses recipients=[] empty path that returns before logging; if no app_owner with email exists the alert silently no-ops with no audit trail.

rca of the issue: BrandingSettingsPage.js used <Upload className='w-4 h-4'/> JSX but the `Upload` symbol was never imported from 'lucide-react'. React rendered the component, hit the unresolved identifier at runtime, threw ReferenceError. Fix: added `Upload` to the existing lucide-react import statement on line 4.
